ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the xOy rectangular coordinate system on a smooth horizontal plane, a small ball with a mass of 1 kg moves uniformly along the positive direction of the x-axis, with a speed of 1 m/s. When it passes through the coordinate origin O, a constant force F that the small ball is subjected to, along the negative direction of the y-axis and with a magnitude of 1 N, is suddenly removed, while the other forces remain unchanged. Then regarding the motion of the small ball, which of the following statements is correct? (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: At the end of 1 s, the speed of the small ball is $\sqrt{2} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure gives the xOy coordinate system, the x-axis is the horizontally rightward direction, the y-axis is the obliquely upper-right direction, and the origin O is at the intersection of the two axes. The small ball is located to the left of O, near the x-axis, with an arrow marked velocity v0 beside it; the arrow points horizontally to the right, indicating that the small ball is moving along the positive direction of the x-axis. Reasoning: The problem statement gives that the mass of the small ball is m=1 kg, and before passing through O it moves uniformly along the positive direction of the x-axis, with speed v0=1 m/s. When it passes through O, a constant force originally acting on it, along the negative direction of the y-axis and with a magnitude of 1 N, is suddenly removed, while the other forces remain unchanged. Before removal, the small ball moves uniformly, indicating that the resultant force is 0; since there is one 1 N constant force along the -y direction, the resultant of the other forces must be 1 N along the +y direction. After this 1 N constant force in the -y direction is removed, the other forces remain unchanged, so the resultant force on the small ball becomes 1 N along the +y direction. By Newton's second law, a_y=F/m=1/1=1 m/s², and there is no acceleration in the x direction, so a_x=0. After 1 s, v_x is still 1 m/s; v_y increases from 0 to a_y t=1×1=1 m/s. The speed is v=sqrt(v_x^2+v_y^2)=sqrt(1^2+1^2)=sqrt(2) m/s.
